title: Allocation and failure checking
goal: Allocate a small array from a validated element count, handle NULL before accessing it, and release the allocation after computing a result.

prerequisites.text: Know arrays, pointers and bounded object lifetimes.
Be able to check an integer before converting it to size_t.

terms.title: Allocation
terms.definition: Obtaining a block of a specified byte size. malloc takes a byte count and returns a pointer or NULL.

terms.title: Size
terms.definition: The number of bytes for count elements. sizeof *values expresses one element's size from its type.

terms.title: Initialization
terms.definition: Writing an initial defined value to each element you use. malloc does not initialize those elements.

sections.title: Why determine the size at runtime
paragraphs: A training program receives a sensor's result count. Runtime allocation can reserve the validated number of integers. The pointer does not carry the length, so retain count separately.
First verify a positive element count and that count times element size fits. Separate the steps: request bytes, check the result, initialize the elements, compute the sum, and release the block.
Here sizeof *values uses the element type. It does not read memory through values. Unlike sizeof, values[0] accesses an object and is valid only after obtaining a block.
The exercise distinguishes controlled refusal from actual memory exhaustion. Flag 0 exercises the NULL path reproducibly with a small request.

sections.title: An array of three elements
paragraphs: Predict the sum after storing 1, 2 and 3. Identify the single path on which the array may be accessed.
steps: Check the byte-size expression before requesting malloc.
Ensure the result is not NULL and initialize the three elements.
Print the sum of 6 and end ownership by calling free.

sections.title: Locate and check the defect
paragraphs: Clang rejects a call to undeclared malloc. Check for stdlib.h. The header supplies the function declaration with the right return type.

If the starter always prints allocation-failed, check that it actually requests memory when the flag permits it. When disabled, the adapter must return NULL before malloc. This refusal is reproducible without exhausting memory.

sections.title: Change, predict and check
paragraphs: Change the example values to 3, 1, 4 and predict the sum. Keep the validation and release sequence.
In the practice, repeat the experiment with flag 0. Record the last reached step and why no element is read.

reading.author: ISO/IEC JTC1/SC22/WG14

selfcheck.prompt: What does the worked example print after successful allocation?
feedback: The elements are initialized before summing.
The element count is not the sum.

selfcheck.prompt: How does handling flag 0 differ from rejecting malformed input?
options: Flag 0 is valid input and prevents the request. Malformed input is rejected earlier.
feedback: Neither branch performs the actual allocation.
NULL is checked before any read.

selfcheck.prompt: Why can neither element access nor a free-memory estimate help in the values == NULL branch?
selfcheck.feedback: There is no block to read. The call has already signaled failure, so report the defined result and finish.

practice.title: A bounded array
practice.task: Enter two whitespace-separated integers on the first line of up to 63 bytes: count from 1 to 16 and a flag of 0 or 1. Later lines are ignored. Complete allocate_values: a denied request or invalid size yields NULL, and an allowed size requests space for count int elements. The supplied main handles NULL. On success it stores 1 through count, prints sum N, and frees the block. Invalid input yields invalid. Flag 0 returns NULL before calling malloc.
criteria: 4 1 gives sum 10, 4 0 gives allocation-failed, and 0 1 gives invalid.
Flag 0 returns from allocate_values before calling malloc. Check NULL before accessing elements. Free each successfully allocated block once.
practice.hint: Use the already validated count. sizeof(int) gives the bytes per element.

steps.action: Run the starter with 4 1. Find the TODO in allocate_values.
steps.why: The request passes validation, but the starter immediately returns NULL.

steps.action: Call malloc after the size check. Run 4 1 and 4 0 separately.
steps.why: The same count distinguishes an actual request from a controlled refusal.
steps.expected: The corrected code prints sum 10 and allocation-failed respectively.

steps.why: Zero is rejected before calling allocate_values.
steps.expected: The results are sum 136 and invalid respectively.

exercises.title: Transfer the idea
exercises.task: Use the positive even numbers 2..2×count and preserve the allocation guard.
criteria: 3 1 gives sum 12, while 3 0 still gives allocation-failed. Explain why the refusal does not depend on the summing formula.

teaching.scene: A measurement collector knows how many values it needs. Separate the memory request from the writes and use both outcomes to check that refusal prevents access.

predict.prompt: The example requests three elements. When malloc succeeds, which values are stored and what prints? How far does execution get if malloc returns NULL?
predict.answer: On success it stores 1, 2 and 3 and prints sum 6, then frees the block. With NULL it prints allocation-failed, then returns before writing.

apply.prompt: Consider requests 6 1 and 6 0. What output demonstrates both successful initialization and controlled refusal without accessing the block?
apply.answer: On successful allocation, 6 1 produces sum 21 by adding 1 through 6. 6 0 gives allocation-failed. The flag refuses the request before malloc.

practice.strategy: Check the flag, positive size and product before requesting storage. Check the returned address, initialize all used slots and release the block.
practice.diagnosis: For 4 1 the starter prints allocation-failed even though the request passed validation. Find out whether the final branch returns the address from malloc.

syntax.explanation: malloc from <stdlib.h> requests bytes. sizeof *values gives the size of one int. Check the returned pointer for NULL before writing.
syntax.mistake: malloc leaves the element values uninitialized. Store every value you intend to read or sum.
